edge_explainer: TAPE: the queue's distribution date is wrong by five sessions. The 8-K of 07-06 states 'On July 6, 2026, The Middleby Corporation completed its spin-off of Midera Food Processing, Inc.'; 06-29 was the CREDIT AGREEMENT CLOSING, not the distribution. The 13D independently confirms the record date (4:00pm CT 06-26), the 1:1 ratio, and that 'the Common Stock commenced trading on The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC on July 7, 2026'. The IBKR tape corroborates exactly: 82,142 / 28,572 / 105,728 / 148,377 / 89,135 shares from 06-29 to 07-06 (when-issued, ticker MFPVV), then 2,312,906 on 07-07. Every generator metric — first_close 35.00, early_high 40.00, trough 35.00, +37% — is a when-issued artifact. Clean regular-way series: $36.60 first close (07-07) -> $47.29 = +29.2% in 19 sessions, with no trough after day 1. 28 days out, not 35. OUR OWN TRADE, re-measured: bought 150 at $35.50 day 1, exited day 3 at ~$39.61 for +11.5% / +$613; held to today the same shares are +$1,768 (+33.2%). We captured 35% of the move. DOCTRINE CONTRADICTION WORTH BANKING: the generator's doctrine says 'the durable edge is the DISCRETIONARY orphan drift over the following 4-8 weeks, not the mechanical print', while our execution rule said 'never marry the flow' and exited on day 3. They point in opposite directions and on this observation (FLOW cohort datapoint #1) the doctrine was right. One datapoint does not change a rule, but the cohort's post-day-3 drift should be measured explicitly rather than left to habit. FLOW: 2.31M shares on regular-way day 1 = 5.1% of shares outstanding in one session, then an uninterrupted 19-session grind higher on decaying volume — a mechanical sell that cleared on day 1 and a discretionary re-rating afterwards. CAP STRUCTURE: 45,214,588 shares; a $1.0B five-year senior SECURED facility ($750M USD + $250M multi-currency revolver, BofA agent, accordion = greater of $151M and 100% of consolidated EBITDA) with only $252.0M DRAWN; $229.0M cash distribution to Middleby; $13.466M/yr pro forma interest at 4.75%; no dividend; emerging growth company. Gross leverage ~1.7x with $748M undrawn — Middleby did NOT strip this one. Read the drawn/undrawn split and the accordion and this is a PLATFORM capitalization, not an extraction (contrast FDXF: $4.1B dividended out, negative equity). THE FINDING THE PRIOR UNDERWRITE MISSED ENTIRELY: SC 13D filed 2026-07-14 by Garden Investment Management LP, GI SPV I LP, GI SPV I GP LLC, Garden Investment Management GP LLC and EDWARD P. GARDEN (Trian co-founder) — 3,380,845 shares = 7.5%, acquired in the spin, with GIM's stated business being 'long-term capital appreciation primarily through investments in The Middleby Corporation and the Issuer'. Critically: 'effective as of immediately prior to the consummation of the Spin-Off, Brian Jacoby, Founding Partner and Head of Research at GIM, was appointed to serve as a member of the board of directors of the Issuer.' Item 4 reserves proposals on operations, governance, capital structure, capital allocation policy, management compensation and corporate strategy. An inside-the-tent activist with a research-partner director, 7.5% of the economics, 1.7x leverage and $748M of dry powder is a materially different asset from 'a fairly-valued food-processing-equipment cyclical in a margin trough'. HYPOTHESIS RAISED AND KILLED: the eleven Forms 4 filed 08-03 into a +29% move looked like an insider-selling cluster; contemporaneous headlines and the 07-02 S-8 identify them as post-spin RSU GRANTS. Routine, not distribution. THE BUSINESS: FY25 (year ended 01-03-2026) net sales $853M — equipment and installation $512M (60%), AFTERMARKET PARTS AND SERVICE $341M (40%) — net earnings $83M (9.7%), adjusted EBITDA $152M (17.8%); 29 manufacturing sites (13 US, 16 across Denmark, France, Germany, India, Italy, Sweden, UK); 56% US/Canada, 44% international; protein and bakery processors. A 40% aftermarket mix is genuinely defensive and the prior underwrite under-weighted it. THE GUIDANCE EXISTS, AND TWO OF MY OWN FINDINGS ARE REFUTED. I wrote that MFP had published no financial targets of any kind and that no standalone cost figure existed. Both are FALSE. An 82-slide Midera investor deck carries full guidance: FY2026 net sales $915-945M (vs FY25 $853M, +7.3% to +10.8%) with segment Adj. EBITDA $186-208M (slide 66) and STANDALONE Adj. EBITDA $154-176M (slide 75). The two bases reconcile exactly — the $32M difference at both ends IS the standalone public-company cost load, quantified, and 28% ABOVE the top of my $15-25M estimate. Both errors came from stopping at the information statement instead of finding the deck, which is exactly the failure the MBGL 'always pull the pre-spin deck alongside the Form 10' rule exists to prevent. THE HONESTY FINDING: the deck markets a '~500 basis point uplift' to a 20-23% margin by 2028, but estimated standalone margin was 21.3% in 2024A and 16.4% in 2025A — the uplift is measured off the depressed 2025 base and merely RETURNS the business to where it already was in 2024. Two independent routes reach this (segment margin history 19.8-25.6% since 2019; the standalone reconciliation 21.3% -> 16.4%). A RECOVERY TARGET SOLD AS AN EXPANSION TARGET — and the correction that most matters to our own 'margin trough' framing. SECOND, UNRECONCILED TENSION: slide 63's M&A algorithm guides 'M&A Velocity ~3-5 deals per year' at '~$25-$50M' each against ~35 identified targets at '~11% EBITDA margin', into a 16-20% base — structurally DILUTIVE on entry, which is precisely what compressed 2025 — yet the 20-23% 2028E target explicitly 'Excludes contribution from future acquisitions.' Executing the stated velocity ($75-250M/yr against >$700M of capacity under a sub-3x ceiling) would hold REPORTED margin below the 20-23% path even if the organic bridge works perfectly. The margin target and the M&A-velocity target cannot both be read off reported results, and the deck never reconciles them. Q1-2026 ACTUALS (slide 69): segment net sales $224M (+34%, organic +29.1%), Adj. EBITDA $41M (+38%), margin 18.5% vs 17.9%, orders $231M (+25%), backlog $416M (+52%). BUT the nuance cuts against the headline: backlog went $410M (Q4-25) -> $416M (Q1-26), only +$6M SEQUENTIALLY, while the quarter shipped $224M — book-to-bill ~1.03x. The +52% is against a depressed Q1-25 base of $274M, and the organic surge is substantially BACKLOG CONVERSION of tariff-delayed orders releasing, not a step-change in demand. Also: ~1% share of a fragmented ~$70B TAM; no forward non-GAAP reconciliation anywhere ('cannot be reasonably estimated' on every target slide); no EPS, standalone-ROIC, tax-rate or working-capital target; no dividend and no buyback anywhere across all 82 slides. VALUATION: $2.138B cap, net debt ~$200M, EV ~$2.34B; 2.50x FY26E sales; 15.4x FY25 EBITDA and 14.2x the FY26E STANDALONE guide midpoint of $165M — the right anchor — against a food-equipment comp range of roughly 9-13x (Marel was taken out at ~13x). Even at the top of the FY26 guide ($176M) it is 13.3x, still at the ceiling. Standalone EPS bridge ~$1.95 -> ~24x. The edge got MORE negative once the deck was read: more data pulled the number down, not up.
